chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a sale in which there is a measure or weight, he estimates it, then takes it upon an approximation of whatever is in it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy goods sold by estimation without knowing the exact quantity?
ai.summary: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about purchasing goods sold by estimation (takhmin) where the buyer accepts the item as is, even if the exact weight or measure is unknown. The Imam’s affirmation of 'no harm' (la ba'sa bihi) establishes the validity of this common commercial practice, provided the essential elements of the contract are clear and the uncertainty (gharar) is not excessive. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that moderate uncertainty in quantity does not invalidate a sale if the parties consent to the risk.
